post.description:
Switch a subject between managed (PRAMPTA signs) and self (you sign)
custody. Only the subject's owner may do this.

→ managed: the server generates a fresh keypair and stores it encrypted.
→ self: you supply a public key you control + proof-of-possession.

Either way the subject's public key changes, but previously issued licenses
keep their own stored signing key, so they still verify.

Add a reserved / high-profile name (operator only). Matching registrations
then go to manual review.

get.description:
Machine-readable subject detection index.

Providers poll this to know WHICH subjects to look for in prompts before
calling /verify (see docs/licensing-integration.md). Includes every
registration regardless of status — withdrawn/disputed subjects must
still be detected (they produce hard refusals), and private subjects
must be detected so the provider knows a license is required.

Exposes only what detection needs: canonical id + aliases + status.
ETag/If-None-Match supported so a cached index costs one cheap 304.

patch.description:
Edit a subject's settings. Only a controller of the subject may do this.
Identity (subject_id, public key) is immutable; everything here is policy
/ presentation that the rights holder can tune anytime.

delete.description:
Hard-delete a subject the caller owns — but ONLY if it was never licensed.

A subject with issued licenses is part of the permanent, verifiable record:
deleting it would break the signed licenses people hold. That case is refused
(409) — the owner should PAUSE it (stop new generation, reversible) or
withdraw it (terminal) instead. Deletion is for cleaning up mistakes and
never-used registrations.

put.description:
Set or clear a subject's portrait. Only a controller of the subject
(operator admin, the personal owner, or an admin of the owning org) may
do this.

Set or clear a subject's preview banner. Only a controller of the subject
(operator admin, the personal owner, or an admin of the owning org) may.

get.description:
Usage analytics for a subject the caller controls: how many times it was
checked for generation, how many were allowed vs refused, and a recent
timeline of who tried, when, and the outcome. Built from the tamper-evident
audit log (verify_allowed / verify_refused events).

List active subjects. Private subjects are always redacted unless the
requester controls them — there is no public bypass.

With ``owned=true`` the result is scoped to subjects the caller actually
OWNS or co-manages (their personal subjects + subjects of orgs where they
are owner/admin). This deliberately ignores the operator (global admin)
override so the profile's "My subjects" shows a user's own registrations
only — an operator does not see everyone's subjects there. The Library
(owned=false) is unchanged.

put.description: Replace a subject's gallery (up to 5 images). Only a controller may.

patch.description:
Transition subject status with authority proof.

Allowed transitions:
- active → disputed (admin/third-party dispute)
- active → withdrawn (subject self-withdrawal, requires signature)
- disputed → active (dispute resolved, requires admin)
- disputed → withdrawn (dispute led to removal)
- pending → active (registration approved)

post.description:
File a dispute against a subject (marks as disputed, blocks generation).

Only admins or the subject owner can file disputes directly.
Third-party disputes should go through a separate review process.

Rotate a subject's Ed25519 public key.

Requires dual proof-of-possession: the rotation message must be signed
by BOTH the old key (proves current ownership) and the new key (proves
the caller holds the new private key). This prevents key replacement
attacks where an attacker who compromises the account but not the
signing key tries to swap it.

DEPRECATED: use /licenses/issue-presigned. That path supports the full
policy (channels/territories/rules_text), records an audit event, and returns

patch.description:
Pause, resume (→active), or revoke a license. Allowed for the subject side
(owner / subject-org admin / operator) or the licensee org admin — the same
parties who may revoke. 'paused' is reversible; 'revoked' is terminal.

get.description:
List active licenses, scoped to what the caller may see. Operators see all;
others see licenses for subjects they control or held by their licensee ids.

Licenses granted TO the current user (licensee side).

Resolves the user's licensee identities (their orgs + personal licensee) plus
any groups those identities belong to, and returns the active licenses for
them — with usage/remaining for volume-capped licenses and expiry.

post.description:
Issue a license using a client-side pre-computed Ed25519 signature.

Flow:
1. Client generates canonical JSON of license body
2. Client signs with subject's Ed25519 private key (WebCrypto)
3. Client submits body + signature_hex here
4. Server verifies signature against registered public key
5. Server countersigns and stores license

Pre-issuance check: warn about rules_text terms that won't be enforced at
runtime because they're not in the structured policy. Advisory only.

DEPRECATED: Use /licenses/issue-presigned instead.
This endpoint accepts raw private keys and is only available in development.
Add an exception to a license (requires subject signature).

Same visibility rule as GET /licenses/{id}: the operator, the subject side
(owner / org-admin), or the holding licensee side. Exceptions are contract

Revoke an exception.

Only the granting side may take it back: the subject's owner (who signed
the exception into existence) or an operator. A licensee cannot revoke —

post.description:
Approve a license request and issue the signed license for it.

The subject or delegated org private key still signs client-side. This
endpoint verifies that signature, stores the license, marks the request as
licensed, and returns a Movie-safe redirect URL only after verify can pass.

Approve a (direct, non-connected) license request and mint its signed
license — to the requester's personal licensee, with terms from the requested
use case. Managed subjects sign server-side (one tap); self-custody subjects
must include subject_signature_hex. Owner-only.

Check if a decision nonce was consumed (issued by this server).

Requires valid pair auth to prevent unauthenticated enumeration.
Returns consumed=True if the nonce was legitimately issued.

Initiate or immediately establish a pair between provider and licensee orgs.

If both orgs exist and the user is a member of one:
- If user belongs to BOTH orgs → pair activated immediately (self-pair)
- If user belongs to ONE org → pair created as pending, counterparty must confirm

Legacy behavior: if orgs don't exist yet, creates pair directly (for backward compat).
This will be removed once org migration is complete.

patch.description:

Returns the pair access token upon successful confirmation.

Rotate an active pair token.

Pair tokens are only shown once and only their SHA-256 hash is stored. This
endpoint invalidates the previous token and returns the new token once.

List pending pair requests that the current user can confirm.

subject signature — an opt-out is consent and cannot be lifted by anyone.

This endpoint accepts raw private keys and is only available in development.

Verify the tamper-evident hash chain and operator signatures.

Bounded to the most recent `limit` events (not the unbounded full chain) so it
can't be used as a DoS lever; operators can page further with `limit`.

Export a self-contained, operator-signed audit bundle for a subject so a
third party can independently verify: license signatures, the hash-chained

get.description: List active organizations.

Contexts the user can act as: personal + real (standard) orgs they belong to.

Auto-provisioned identities (personal-licensee, Connect-AI service providers)
are excluded — they are infrastructure, not selectable contexts.

Echo the validated acting context for the current X-Org-Context header.

Returns the personal context when no (or empty) header is sent; 400/403 if
the header references an invalid org or one the user doesn't belong to.

Capability check: 200 only when acting as a domain-verified org.

The frontend uses this to gate verified-org-only features. Returns 403 when
acting personally or as an unverified org.
List organizations the current user belongs to.
Get organization details.

patch.description:
Update editable org fields (admin+). Used to set the domain before
verification. A verified domain cannot be changed.

post.description:
Register the org's delegated Ed25519 signing key (admin, proof-of-possession).

Org-owned subjects are bound to this one key; the org signs their licenses with
it. The private key never leaves the org — only a proof signature is sent.

Rotate the org's delegated signing key to a NEW key (admin only).

Proves possession of the NEW key only — you can't prove a lost/compromised
old key, and requiring it would block rotation exactly when it's needed.
Subjects bound to the old org key are repointed to the new key so FUTURE
licenses sign with it; already-issued licenses keep verifying against their
snapshotted key, so nothing in circulation breaks.

patch.description:
Mark an organization as a trusted issuer (KYB / contracted partner).

Operator-only — this is the out-of-band KYB decision made when a partner
(e.g. a talent agency) signs a contract. A trusted issuer's bulk
registrations auto-activate (reserved / high-profile names still reviewed).

post.description:
Register many subjects at once, bound to the org's delegated signing key.

Requires: admin role, a domain-verified org, and a signing key already set.
No per-subject proof is needed — the org key was proven once via
/signing-key, and these subjects are bound to it (delegated signing).
